newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates edge up for Mideast/east routes.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates edge up for Mideast/east routes.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) travelling east from the Middle East were steady to firmer on Tuesday, shipping brokers said.
Ssangyong fixed at least two 260,000 tonne vessels from the Middle East to South Korea in mid to late December at W60, while Kyushu fixed the 250,000 tonne World Phoenix for Japan at W67.5.
Westwards routes from the Middle East were quieter, however, amid a dearth of fixtures. Offers for VLCCs from the Mideast to the U.S. Gulf were heard at W62.
West African markets were busy and a VLCC was heard fixed at W62.5 to the U.S. Gulf, while another two-million-barrel ship was chartered at just over W63 for Canada.

But the improving West African activity was causing a dearth of tonnage for potential charterers for North Sea/transatlantic movements. Million-barrel rates were pegged notionally at W107.5 for North Sea/USAC routes.

Mediterranean markets for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes and 80,000 tonne Aframaxes were calm and brokers saw room for further downwards movement for cross-Med routes. "It has been quiet for a couple of days and people are nervous," one broker said.
While rates for Aframaxes were pegged at around W107.5, one broker said he feared that a lack of activity was likely to push the numbers down towards W100.

Iraq's senior under-secretary to the oil ministry said on Tuesday he thought 350,000 barrels of oil could be exported daily from the offshore terminal of Mina al Bakr under its oil-for-food deal with the U.N. An additional 450,000 barrels per day of Iraqi oil could be exported from the Turkish port of Ceyhan, he added.
